_comment: Coordinates geocoded via OpenStreetMap Nominatim (2026-09-12). Chokepoints named directly in news coverage of the Sep 11 2026 exodus and prior-year recurrences.

corridors.name: Tumkur Road / NH48 (Peenya-Goraguntepalya)
corridors.evidence: Repeatedly named as gridlocked (Goraguntepalya Jn, Peenya flyover) in 2025/2026 Ganesh Chaturthi coverage

corridors.name: Nelamangala Toll Plaza
corridors.evidence: 4km+ jam reported at this toll plaza ahead of Ganesh Chaturthi long weekend

corridors.name: Mysore Road (NH275)
corridors.evidence: Named as heavily congested well into the night on Sep 11 2026

corridors.name: Bengaluru-Mysuru Highway Toll Plaza (Sheshagirihalli/Kaniminike area)
corridors.evidence: Kilometre-long queues reported at Kaniminike and Sheshagirihalli toll plazas during the festival weekend

corridors.name: Kanakapura Road
corridors.evidence: Named among the exit routes heavily congested on Sep 11 2026

corridors.name: Hosur Road / Silk Board Junction
corridors.direction: Bengaluru → Electronic City / Hosur / Tamil Nadu
corridors.evidence: Named among the exit routes heavily congested on Sep 11 2026; also Bengaluru's most chronic year-round chokepoint, useful as a baseline-congestion control point

reference_point.name: Kempegowda Bus Station (Majestic)
reference_point.note: Central reference point — the mobbed bus stand at the center of the exodus, not itself a polled corridor
